Hospital Name: Summit Health System
Department: Gastroenterology
Patient Name: Robert Sterling
MRN: RS1234567
DOB: 11/08/1965
Age: 58
Sex: Male
Encounter Date: 05/20/2024
Document Type: Endoscopy Report
Provider: Dr. Michael Vance, MD

Preoperative Diagnosis: History of positive fecal occult blood test; rule out colonic polyps/neoplasia.

Postoperative Diagnosis: Diverticulosis; hyperplastic polyp, sigmoid colon.

Procedure Performed: Colonoscopy, flexible, diagnostic; with collection of specimen(s) by brushing or washing.

Primary Surgeon: Dr. Michael Vance, MD

Anesthesia Type: Moderate Sedation (Fentanyl and Midazolam)

Indications for Procedure: Patient is a 58-year-old male with a recent positive fecal occult blood test. No personal history of colon cancer, but family history of colon polyps. Patient reports no changes in bowel habits or rectal bleeding.

Description of Procedure:
After obtaining informed consent, the patient was placed in the left lateral decubitus position. Moderate sedation was administered, and the patient tolerated the procedure well. A flexible colonoscope (Olympus CF-HQ190L) was inserted into the rectum and advanced under direct visualization through the sigmoid colon, descending colon, transverse colon, ascending colon, and into the cecum. The terminal ileum was not intubated. Bowel preparation was excellent, allowing for clear visualization of the mucosa.

Findings:
RECTUM: Normal mucosa. No hemorrhoids or masses.
SIGMOID COLON: Multiple small diverticula noted. A 3 mm sessile, pale polyp was identified approximately 30 cm from the anal verge. This was biopsied using cold forceps, and the specimen was sent for pathology. No other lesions.
DESCENDING COLON: Normal mucosa. No polyps or diverticula.
TRANSVERSE COLON: Normal mucosa. No polyps or diverticula.
ASCENDING COLON: Normal mucosa. No polyps or diverticula.
CECUM: Normal mucosa. Appendiceal orifice identified.

Specimens: One specimen (sigmoid polyp biopsy) sent to pathology.

Complications: None.

Disposition: Patient recovered well from sedation and was discharged home with post-procedure instructions. Follow-up with gastroenterology in 2 weeks to discuss pathology results.

Electronically Signed By:
Dr. Michael Vance, MD
Gastroenterologist

Date Signed: 05/20/2024 15:10

End of Report
